question: Participation in a structured cardiac rehabilitation programme after MI has been shown to reduce cardiovascular mortality by approximately 20–25%.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is true. Exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation reduces cardiovascular mortality by 20–25% and all-cause mortality by a similar magnitude, with additional benefits in exercise capacity, quality of life, and depression. It is a Class I recommendation for post-MI patients.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Meta-analyses of exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation consistently show a 20–25% reduction in cardiovascular mortality and a significant reduction in re-hospitalisation rates. CR is recommended in all post-ACS patients (Class I evidence).
